preflight: refuse to let a shallow clone pass unmentioned

scripts/science_preflight.py exists because an outside environment breaks
assumptions silently. It checked the interpreter, the ball-arithmetic backend,
plotting, Lean and the next free doc number, and not the one that cost this
session most.

The container this ran in held 262 commits of 1094 and said nothing. Files are
current on a shallow clone, so nothing reads stale and nothing warns. Two things
it ruins: any measurement over history (a study of how often a claim gets
revised reported 30.5% never-revisited against a true 23.2%, and 95.8% at depth
100), and the appearance of a green suite, because
tests/test_dossier_hardy_z.py skips on truncated history by design. Completing
the clone turned that test red on a staleness five days old.

A warning rather than a block, because most work here needs no history. It is a
block only for the thing it silently ruins, and the verdict line now says which
kind of "ready" you have.

Fired on a real shallow clone before landing: git clone --depth 5 file://,
5 commits, and the section prints and the verdict changes. Silent on the
complete one.

preflight: the history check no longer fails open

Lands the shallow-clone check from claude/repo-hunt-content-2smbid (1db6ad987,
the previous commit) with the defect a review found in it. When git could not
answer, which is the case on a snapshot mounted without .git, the environment
this preflight exists for, _check_history printed one line and returned no
warning, so the verdict read "Ready. Every claim this repository knows how to
make is available." Reproduced before the fix with GIT_DIR pointing nowhere.

Every way of not knowing the history is now a WARNING with exit 0, the same
kind as a shallow clone: git missing, git failing, git answering for an
enclosing repository (a snapshot unpacked inside one, whose history would
otherwise be counted as this tree's), and a git too old to say whether the
clone is shallow. The verdict then reads "Ready for work that does not read
git history".

Also: the imports are alphabetical again, the module docstring names truncated
history among the silent breakages and says what exit 0 with a warning means,
the section is labelled 3b because it prints after section 3, and CLAUDE.md's
description of the preflight names the history check.

tests/test_science_preflight.py (8 tests, about a second) runs the check
against throwaway repositories: a complete history gives no warning, a real
--depth 1 clone warns, and each unreadable case warns. Five planted faults (the
original fail-open return, no toplevel check, no answer check, shallow
detection off, a verdict that ignores the warnings) each turn red exactly the
test written to catch it. CONTEXT.md regenerated for the new test file.

Run by hand: this worktree reports complete, 1615 commits, and "Ready. Every
claim ...". A depth-5 clone (8 commits), GIT_DIR=/nonexistent, git off PATH, a
copy of the tree without .git, and that copy inside another repository each
give a WARNING and exit 0.

rung 3: the strip theorems carry the result; davenport_heilbronn is met by s = -1

An adversarial review of this landing found that
davenport_heilbronn_statement asks only for a zero with Re s != 1/2. The
trivial zero s = -1 meets it: both characters in DH are odd, so their
L-functions vanish there. The headline theorem therefore needed none of
the 215 sites, and as stated it does not separate DH from zeta, which has
a trivial zero at s = -2.

weil_dh_line: raise K2 at the DH line to every T#: the 856-mode DH form in position space has a negative eigenvalue

The stage-A block R(T#) increases to the N-mode DH form Q_N as T# grows, so
the pipeline refuses DH at L_DH at every T# exactly when Q_N has a negative
eigenvalue. witness.py assembles Q_856 with no T# split, through the explicit
formula in position space, in Arb (exact Gauss sums for the correlations, an
Arb-bounded Gauss-Legendre error for the archimedean integral, carried bounds
for dropped radii and comb mass; eps 6.0e-64).

- Q_856 has one negative eigenvalue, -1.94308362498e-30; the stored witness
  has an enclosed Rayleigh quotient <= -1.9430836249e-30. Every leading block
  from 101 modes on is negative (onset between 100 and 101), and an
  independent assembly of Q_101 reproduces its witness to 15 digits.
- Calibrated against the hunt's stored C(800) block (agreement to the tail
  beyond 800, 1e-38) and the CCM closed forms (below 4e-60); planted faults
  move the form by 0.012 to 1.6.
- The T# = 800 eigenvector is not a witness: Q_856 there is +6.366e-30; its
  refusal was the discarded boundary tail (1.05e-29).
- Stage A at T# = 800 with honest radii: v^T R(800) v enclosed at
  -4.15160674833728e-30 by a route independent of the stored state and the
  Bessel column; t-quadrature bounded (8e-89).
- S lesion: the T# = 800 verdict flips between dS = 43 and 44; K2 does not
  test S. Refusal at every T# >= 800 survives S low by any delta < 13.66.
- Honest responses (scout.responses_of rounds the data); the archimedean bound
  for beta* is proved (Binet) instead of grid-checked.
- PRICE.md: the reasoning chain graded link by link (E_856 negative: hardened;
  E = Q: derivation, unreviewed, calibration measured; refusal at every T#:
  measured at the validity of S), corrections dated, doors and the two
  unlaunched runs priced. RUNS.md: manifests and estimates.

weil_dh_line: the envelope constant S bounded in Arb; K2 refusal at every T# >= 540 (N >= 856) with no measured step

The refusal at every T# rested on S >= sup(P_DH - H), proved by joint.py's
branch-and-bound only under an IEEE 754 rounding model. The witness's margin
needs much less: S_true <= S_used + delta with delta below |Q(v)| / m_T(v).

- joint.arb_sup_bound: branch-and-bound over a cluster's half torus with
  centre values, gradients and the second-order Taylor remainder all in Arb
  (128 bits); price.arb_envelope_bound runs it per cluster, checks the weight
  cover exactly and adds the dropped comb mass.
- Result: sup(P_DH - H) <= S_used + 34/5 (and <= S_used + 12), every cluster
  proved at U_c + (5/2, 1, 23/10, 1); about 0.3 core-hours in all (timed and
  priced first, RUNS.md). The trivial l1 bound would give 111.7.
- The witness's tail mass from 540, enclosed by the single-vector route:
  m_540 <= 2.4514738e-31, so v^T R(T#) v / |v|^2 <= -1.9431e-30 + 6.8 m_540
  = -2.76e-31 at every T# >= 540 for N >= 856.
- Regrade (PRICE.md item 7, link 6): every numerical step of the refusal at
  T# >= 540, N >= 856 is enclosed or bounded; it rests on two derivations
  (links 2 and 4) that stay unreviewed. For 101 <= N < 856 and
  527.5 < T# < 540 it still assumes a valid S.
- Tests: the recorded bounds and margin arithmetic, a live Arb re-proof of one
  cluster, and a planted target below the supremum that must fail.

@@ -0,0 +1,169 @@
+# Hunt #119 lambda_dh_exact: the landing census over [1e4, 1e5] (hunts/lambda_dh_exact/).
+#
+# Triggered ONLY by a push to hunt/lambda-dh-exact-resume that touches
+# hunts/lambda_dh_exact/RUN_REQUEST.json; never by this file. The request is
+# committed only after the coordinator's 'go' (RUNS.md, "The 1e5 census on
+# Actions"): first {"mode": "calibrate"}, then {"mode": "full"} sized from the
+# calibration. The pre-registration is RESULTS.md section 8.12.
+#
+# RUN_REQUEST.json: {"mode": "calibrate" | "full", "attempt": <int>,
+#                    "plan_sha256": <sha256 of census_plan_1e5.json>,
+#                    "calibrate_shard": <int, calibrate mode, default 18>}
+#
+# Jobs: plan (reads the request) -> shards (each job: fail-closed preflight,
+# then 4 shards of census_plan_1e5.json in 4 processes, or shard 0 alone in
+# calibrate mode) -> merge (full mode; refuses a missing shard or one from
+# another plan).
+#
+# Modes:
+#   calibrate  job 0 runs one shard alone ("calibrate_shard", default 18 =
+#              [55000, 57500], mid-decade height and mean zero density; one
+#              process, so its CPU seconds are not shared) and writes calibration.json: CPU seconds per
+#              screened 20-unit window and per census window, and the
+#              projected core-hours for all 36 shards.
+#   full       9 jobs x 4 processes = 36 shards, max-parallel 4.
+#
+# Resume: census_shard.py run is idempotent (the screen resumes from its
+# checkpoint, the census skips rows already landed). A re-run attempt
+# downloads this job's artifacts from the earlier attempts of the same request
+# and continues. Artifact names carry the request's "attempt" and
+# github.run_attempt, so no two attempts collide.
+name: lambda-dh-census
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - "hunt/lambda-dh-exact-resume"
+    paths:
+      - "hunts/lambda_dh_exact/RUN_REQUEST.json"
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: lambda-dh-census
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+# bash -eo pipefail for every run step: a failing command piped into tee
+# (the calibration record) must fail its step, not go green with no numbers
+defaults:
+  run:
+    shell: bash
+
+env:
+  PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"
+  OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"
+  OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS: "1"
+  MKL_NUM_THREADS: "1"
+  FLINT_NUM_THREADS: "1"
+  LD: hunts/lambda_dh_exact
+
+jobs:
+  plan:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    outputs:
+      mode: ${{ steps.p.outputs.mode }}
+      jobs: ${{ steps.p.outputs.jobs }}
+      req: ${{ steps.p.outputs.req }}
+      cal: ${{ steps.p.outputs.cal }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - id: p
+        run: |
+          python3 - <<'PY' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          import json
+          req = json.load(open("hunts/lambda_dh_exact/RUN_REQUEST.json"))
+          plan = json.load(open("hunts/lambda_dh_exact/census_plan_1e5.json"))
+          mode = req["mode"]
+          assert mode in ("calibrate", "full"), mode
+          assert isinstance(req["attempt"], int) and req["attempt"] >= 1, req
+          assert len(plan["shards"]) == 36, len(plan["shards"])
+          print("mode=" + mode)
+          print("req=" + str(req["attempt"]))
+          cal = int(req.get("calibrate_shard", 18))
+          assert 0 <= cal < 36, cal
+          print("cal=" + str(cal))
+          print("jobs=" + json.dumps([0] if mode == "calibrate" else list(range(9))))
+          PY
+
+  shards:
+    name: shards ${{ matrix.job }} (${{ needs.plan.outputs.mode }})
+    needs: plan
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 350
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      max-parallel: 4
+      matrix:
+        job: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs) }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with: {python-version: "3.12", cache: pip}
+      - name: install (exact versions from census_constraints.txt)
+        run: |
+          python -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check -c "$LD/census_constraints.txt" -r requirements.txt
+          python -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check --no-deps -e .
+      - name: resume (re-run attempts only)
+        if: ${{ fromJSON(github.run_attempt) > 1 }}
+        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          pattern: lambda-dh-census-r${{ needs.plan.outputs.req }}-job${{ matrix.job }}-attempt*
+          path: prior/
+      - name: gather the most advanced copy of each shard (re-run attempts only)
+        if: ${{ fromJSON(github.run_attempt) > 1 }}
+        run: python "$LD/census_shard.py" gather --src prior --out out
+      - name: preflight (fail closed; pins, ball backend, plan hash, smoke row)
+        run: python "$LD/census_shard.py" preflight
+      - name: run shards
+        run: |
+          mkdir -p out
+          if [ "${{ needs.plan.outputs.mode }}" = calibrate ]; then
+            SHARDS="${{ needs.plan.outputs.cal }}"
+          else
+            SHARDS="$(( 4 * ${{ matrix.job }} )) $(( 4 * ${{ matrix.job }} + 1 )) $(( 4 * ${{ matrix.job }} + 2 )) $(( 4 * ${{ matrix.job }} + 3 ))"
+          fi
+          for s in $SHARDS; do
+            timeout 335m python "$LD/census_shard.py" run --shard "$s" --out out > "out/log_$s.txt" 2>&1 &
+          done
+          status=0
+          for j in $(jobs -p); do wait "$j" || status=$?; done
+          tail -n 3 out/log_*.txt
+          echo "exit status $status" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+          exit $status
+      - name: calibration record (calibrate mode)
+        if: ${{ always() && needs.plan.outputs.mode == 'calibrate' }}
+        run: |
+          python "$LD/census_shard.py" calib --shard "${{ needs.plan.outputs.cal }}" --out out | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        if: always()
+        with:
+          name: lambda-dh-census-r${{ needs.plan.outputs.req }}-job${{ matrix.job }}-attempt${{ github.run_attempt }}
+          path: out/
+          if-no-files-found: warn
+
+  merge:
+    name: merge the 36 shards
+    needs: [plan, shards]
+    if: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.mode == 'full' }}
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with: {python-version: "3.12"}
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          pattern: lambda-dh-census-r${{ needs.plan.outputs.req }}-job*
+          path: prior/
+      - name: merge (most advanced copy per shard; refuses a missing shard or one from another plan)
+        run: |
+          python "$LD/census_shard.py" gather --src prior --out out
+          python "$LD/census_shard.py" merge --out out
+          sha256sum out/census_1e5.json | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: lambda-dh-census-r${{ needs.plan.outputs.req }}-merged-attempt${{ github.run_attempt }}
+          path: out/census_1e5.json

+# Rung 3 production: the 215 sites of plan v2 (lean/cert/rung3_plan2.json), each
+# compiled to a kernel-checked site theorem under `scripts/60 --tower whole`
+# (hunts/rung3_ball_production/, PRODUCTION.md; PILOT.md section 9).
+#
+# Triggered ONLY by a push to hunt/rung3-ball-production that touches
+# hunts/rung3_ball_production/RUN_REQUEST.json, which carries the run parameters;
+# never by this file. The request is committed only after the coordinator's 'go':
+# first {"mode": "calibrate"}, then the full run.
+#
+# Modes (RUN_REQUEST.json "mode"; production.py validates the request):
+#   calibrate  job 0 only: request["sites"] (the centre, K = 361, the largest site,
+#              and one small site), one Lean process at a time, so each site's CPU,
+#              wall, peak RSS and olean bytes are clean (sites.json in the artifact).
+#   full       request["jobs"] jobs (about 20), sites assigned by projected CPU
+#              (pilot.json whole_projection; about 1.5 core-hours each at the shared
+#              box's rates, every job under 4 h projected), plus the job "fault":
+#              one site with its Prime_<site>_2 radius one unit of 2^-64 low, which the kernel
+#              must refuse at that tower's ev_whole. The verdict job counts the run
+#              only if all 215 sites compiled, every site theorem's axioms are exactly
+#              propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and the fault was refused.
+#   fault      the job "fault" alone, completing a full run whose fault job left no
+#              verdict ("completes_run"); `production.py verdict --runs <full> <fault>`
+#              then takes the sites and axioms from the one and the fault from the other.
+#
+# Each job builds a FRESH lean/.lake with `lake exe cache get` (never a copied
+# .lake: CLAUDE.md compute rule 7); only elan's toolchains and Mathlib's
+# downloaded olean archives (~/.cache/mathlib, keyed on the pinned revision) are
+# cached. Compiles stop themselves at 300 minutes so the artifacts upload inside
+# the 350-minute limit; a re-run attempt downloads this job's earlier artifacts
+# and scripts/72 resumes from their checkpoints.
+name: rung3-production
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - "hunt/rung3-ball-production"
+    paths:
+      - "hunts/rung3_ball_production/RUN_REQUEST.json"
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: rung3-production
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+env:
+  PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"
+  HUNT: hunts/rung3_ball_production
+  REQ: hunts/rung3_ball_production/RUN_REQUEST.json
+  MATHLIB_REV: 065356127b1dc0016f66b7283ce0ce2c4055aa55
+
+jobs:
+  plan:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    outputs:
+      jobs: ${{ steps.p.outputs.jobs }}
+      mode: ${{ steps.p.outputs.mode }}
+      lean_jobs: ${{ steps.p.outputs.lean_jobs }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with: {python-version: "3.12"}
+      - id: p
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          python "$HUNT/production.py" plan --request "$REQ" > plan.txt
+          cat plan.txt
+          sed -n 's/^mode=/mode=/p; s/^jobs=/jobs=/p' plan.txt >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          sed -n 's/^lean_jobs=/lean_jobs=/p' plan.txt >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+  sites:
+    name: sites ${{ matrix.job }} (${{ needs.plan.outputs.mode }})
+    needs: plan
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 350
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      max-parallel: 6
+      matrix:
+        job: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs) }}
+    env:
+      JOB: ${{ matrix.job }}
+      LEAN_JOBS: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.lean_jobs }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with: {python-version: "3.12"}
+
+      - name: free runner disk
+        run: |
+          df -h /
+          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc /usr/local/.ghcup /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL || true
+          sudo docker image prune --all --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+          df -h /
+
+      - name: cache elan toolchains and Mathlib's downloaded olean archives
+        uses: actions/cache@v4
+        with:
+          path: |
+            ~/.elan
+            ~/.cache/mathlib
+          key: rung3-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('lean/lean-toolchain') }}-mathlib-${{ env.MATHLIB_REV }}
+
+      - name: install elan
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leanprover/elan/master/elan-init.sh \
+            | sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain none
+          echo "$HOME/.elan/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
+
+      - name: fresh lean/.lake from the Mathlib cache
+        working-directory: lean
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          test ! -e .lake || { echo "::error::lean/.lake exists before the fetch"; exit 1; }
+          lake --version
+          /usr/bin/time -v lake exe cache get 2>&1 | tail -15
+          df -h /
+
+      - name: preflight (fail closed)
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          python "$HUNT/production.py" toplevels
+          python "$HUNT/production.py" preflight --request "$REQ"
+
+      - name: the ZetaLean closure the sites import
+        working-directory: lean
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          /usr/bin/time -v lake build ZetaLean.BallCertSupport ZetaLean.BallTerm 2>&1 | tail -25
+
+      - name: resume (re-run attempts only)
+        if: ${{ fromJSON(github.run_attempt) > 1 && matrix.job != 'fault' }}
+        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          pattern: rung3-production-job${{ matrix.job }}-attempt*
+          merge-multiple: true
+          path: .                 # the artifact holds out/ and gen/*.manifest.json
+
+      - name: generate this job's sites (--tower whole)
+        if: ${{ matrix.job != 'fault' }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          python "$HUNT/production.py" sites --request "$REQ" --job "$JOB" | tee sites.txt
+          python "$HUNT/production.py" generate --request "$REQ" --job "$JOB" --gen gen
+          ls gen/*.manifest.json | wc -l
+
+      - name: compile (scripts/72, resume-safe)
+        if: ${{ matrix.job != 'fault' }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          mkdir -p out
+          /usr/bin/time -v -o out/time_compile.txt timeout 300m \
+            python scripts/72_rung3_ball_compile.py --lean-project lean --output-root out \
+            --jobs "$LEAN_JOBS" --module-jobs 1 gen/*.manifest.json 2>&1 | tee out/compile.log
+          df -h /
+
+      - name: axioms of every site theorem (exactly the three standard ones)
+        if: ${{ matrix.job != 'fault' }}
+        run: python "$HUNT/production.py" axioms --request "$REQ" --job "$JOB" --gen gen --out out
+
+      - name: plant the fault (one unit of 2^-64 off a tower radius)
+        if: ${{ matrix.job == 'fault' }}
+        run: python "$HUNT/production.py" fault --request "$REQ" --gen gen
+
+      - name: compile the faulted site (must be refused)
+        if: ${{ matrix.job == 'fault' }}
+        # GitHub runs `bash -e {0}`: the compile is meant to fail, so -e is suspended
+        # around it and its exit captured; `refused` then decides (run 40353536947 lost
+        # its fault verdict to -e, PILOT.md section 13).
+        run: |
+          set -u
+          mkdir -p out
+          set +e
+          python scripts/72_rung3_ball_compile.py --lean-project lean --output-root out \
+            --jobs 1 --module-jobs 1 gen/*.manifest.json 2>&1 | tee out/compile.log
+          rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
+          set -e
+          python "$HUNT/production.py" refused --request "$REQ" --gen gen --out out --rc "$rc"
+
+      - name: per-site record (CPU, wall, peak RSS, olean bytes)
+        if: always()
+        run: |
+          mkdir -p out
+          if [ "$JOB" != fault ]; then
+            python "$HUNT/production.py" record --request "$REQ" --job "$JOB" --out out || true
+          fi
+          mkdir -p record
+          cp "$REQ" record/
+          cp out/sites.json out/axioms.json out/fault.json out/time_compile.txt record/ 2>/dev/null || true
+          cp gen/*.manifest.json record/ 2>/dev/null || true
+
+      - name: upload oleans, checkpoints, manifests and logs
+        if: ${{ always() && matrix.job != 'fault' }}
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: rung3-production-job${{ matrix.job }}-attempt${{ github.run_attempt }}
+          path: |
+            out/
+            gen/*.manifest.json
+          if-no-files-found: warn
+          retention-days: 30
+
+      - name: upload the fault job's logs (the refusing declaration, the planted source)
+        if: ${{ always() && matrix.job == 'fault' }}
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: rung3-production-fault-logs-attempt${{ github.run_attempt }}
+          path: |
+            out/compile.log
+            out/logs/
+            out/results/
+            out/fault.json
+            gen/*/Primes.lean
+            gen/*.manifest.json
+          if-no-files-found: warn
+          retention-days: 90
+
+      - name: upload the record
+        if: always()
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: rung3-production-record-job${{ matrix.job }}-attempt${{ github.run_attempt }}
+          path: record/
+          if-no-files-found: warn
+
+  verdict:
+    needs: [plan, sites]
+    if: always()
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with: {python-version: "3.12"}
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          pattern: rung3-production-record-*
+          path: records/
+      - name: count the run (all sites ok, every audit clean, the fault refused)
+        run: python "$HUNT/production.py" verdict --request "$REQ" --records records

+# 46. The Davenport-Heilbronn v6 census: a same-verifier Arb replay
+
+> On 2026-10-24 this laboratory re-ran the published verifier of Nathan Berzai's
+> v6 census of Davenport-Heilbronn zeros (Zenodo, version DOI
+> 10.5281/zenodo.23585903) from scratch on a 32-core Linux host, after replacing
+> its one binary64 step, the disc majorant `M_bound`, by an Arb outward enclosure.
+> All 400 windows and all 1,268 listed off-line zeros recomputed with zero
+> failures and reproduced the census exactly: 1,268 pairs off the line, 25,078
+> zeros on it, 27,614 in total for 0 < Im s < 20,000. This is a full replay with
+> the author's own code, one repaired function, and the same ball-arithmetic
+> library. It is **not** a second independent implementation, not a kernel-checked
+> theorem, and the word this repository reserves for `zeta/rigor.py` does not apply.
+
+## 1. What was replayed, exactly
+
+Upstream artifact. `DH_census_v6_package.zip`, SHA-256
+`c50c0bcef907daa2fdfa30c92f6011edf4ef87eadd6467cf1b6e34eb0565355f`, the single
+file of Zenodo record 23585903 (published 2026-10-23, title "A Certified Census
+of Davenport-Heilbronn Zeros to Height 20,000", v6). Its `CITATION.cff` gives
+`doi: 10.5281/zenodo.21910254`; that is the **concept DOI** resolving to the
+latest version, confirmed against the Zenodo API on 2026-10-24
+(`conceptdoi` 21910254, `doi` 23585903). Cite the version DOI for the bytes
+replayed here and the concept DOI for the catalogue as a living record. Code is
+MIT, data CC-BY 4.0, both (c) 2026 Nathan Berzai; the receipts and tables kept
+here are redistributed under those terms with this attribution.
+
+Inputs pinned. `dh_zeros_master_v6.csv` SHA-256
+`1ce493501c9356cf7bbb433add0a5120b0fed87bc7acdbaedb93e286e8ba4050` (1,268 rows);
+`closure_table.csv` `f4c2601ee5f68eb773c3b73ee293c4b05749898e031b2135b2838cf8094aaf1a`
+(400 windows of height 50); `verify/vdh.py`
+`f8e03d7e69035682d6e574e0f3ac7b5e1b8ffb2247dbae1713efc4a97a964398`;
+`verify/vwin.py` `80b6f9919cc8a0eb1ccae5f1c9c1dd96e10c564f50e23ac60316914a7649e913`.
+
+Environment. Python 3.11.17, python-flint 0.9.0 (Arb/FLINT), mpmath 1.4.1,
+numpy 2.4.6, Linux x86-64, `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, eight
+worker processes. The package scripts carry three hard-coded Windows path
+literals (v6 CSV, closure CSV, v5 CSV); only those were changed in the copy that
+ran. The package ships no v5 file, so the v5 input was a proxy derived from the
+1,232 v6 rows carrying a nonempty `n`; it feeds only the descriptive
+"new since v5" flag, never a count.
+
+The one source change. `vdh.py:74-82` computed the Cauchy-disc majorant
+`M_bound` in binary64 (`math.hypot`, `4.0 ** (-smin)`, a `1.001` margin) and
+converted the float to Arb afterwards. A float is not an upper bound. The
+repaired `vdh.py` (SHA-256
+`471bc0ec9f4d85f92d84e0bf9211eb684f0d5aa8fd705233b1eaedf05dec6666`, 71-line
+normalized diff kept as `vdh_arb_majorant.patch` inside the receipts tarball)
+evaluates the same displayed expression in Arb from the exact centre ball,
+lower-encloses `smin`, proves `smin > -19/20` and `kappa < 2840791/10^7` as
+interval facts, and returns an Arb endpoint enclosure; the Taylor error balls
+are then built from `abs_upper()` of that enclosure, so no Arb value is treated
+as an exact scalar. Every guard and bisection decision in `vwin.py` is
+untouched (`vwin.py` byte-identical to the package copy up to the path
+literals). A descriptive comparison over all 20,000 interior, 401 edge and
+1,268 row centres put the repaired/original ratio in
+[0.999999999999999, 1.0000000000000009]; the ratio is a diagnostic, never a
+certificate of anything.
+
+## 2. What ran and what came out
+
+```
+.venv/bin/python gates.py                                    # exit 0, G0..G3 true
+.venv/bin/python check_bound.py                              # exit 0, 21,669 centres, 0 exceptions
+.venv/bin/python lesion.py                                   # exit 0, fault rejected (section 4)
+.venv/bin/python -u run_fresh.py --workers 8 --seconds 850   # exit 0, wall 729.33 s, 400 receipts
+.venv/bin/python -u certify_rows.py 950 rows_cert.jsonl      # exit 0, wall 173.40 s (after a 60 s first pass)
+python3 summarize.py                                         # exit 0, assertions passed
+```
+
+Results, re-derived in this repository from the raw receipts by
+`scripts/dh_v6_replay_audit.py` (not copied from the worker's summary):
+
+| quantity | value |
+|---|---|
+| window receipts, distinct, `status == computed`, runner exit 0 | 400 / 400 |
+| windows with `N_S != S`, undecided separator sign, or `imag_not_zero` | 0, 0, 0 |
+| sum of `N_R` (off-line pairs by the argument principle) | 1,268 |
+| sum of `N_S` (on-line zeros by sign changes of Z) | 25,078 |
+| total multiplicity `N_S + 2 N_R` | 27,614 |
+| row receipts, distinct, `winding == 1`, verdict confirmed, Rouche radius present | 1,268 / 1,268 |
+| listed rows per window equal to that window's `N_R`, and to `offline_pairs_v6` | 400 / 400 |
+| disagreements with the v6 CSV or closure table | 0 |
+| retries, errors, timeouts, memory stops | 0 |
+
+Every number agrees with the census and with the earlier fresh replays
+(21 + 379 windows without the bound repair, and 1,268 rows). Agreement of
+same-code runs across two majorant implementations is evidence that the float
+majorant was not the weak point in practice; it is not independent validation
+of the algorithm.
+
+## 3. The exact evidence rung
+
+Enclosure-carrying for every numeric step of one verifier: the finite-window
+counts now carry Arb enclosures through the one step that previously did not.
+It stops short of the hardened rung as this repository uses it, because no
+independent route agrees with it, and far short of kernel-checked. Every
+statement below is conditional on the items in section 5.
+
+- Finite range only: `0 < Im s < 20,000`. Nothing above, nothing about any
+  conjecture, and nothing about zeros on `Re s = 1/2` beyond their count.
+- Same verifier, not a second one. The replay exercised the author's
+  `vwin.window` and row routines with one function replaced. There is no
+  independent interval implementation, and the receipts hold aggregate counts
+  and radii, not every accepted contour segment.
+- The analytic majorant is a derived Euler-Maclaurin bound, checked by hand:
+  with `a = m/5`, coefficients `(1, k, -k, -1)` and the periodic-`B2` form of
+  the Hurwitz zeta, the pole terms pair into `(1/5)[int_1^4 x^-s dx + k int_2^3 x^-s dx]`,
+  of modulus at most `(3 + k) J / 5 < 1.4 J` for `0 < k < 0.2840791`, and the
+  remaining terms give the code's bracket with `|B2| <= 1/6` and `|s| <= S`.
+  This derivation lives in a review note, not a proof kernel. The lab checked
+  the pole-pairing arithmetic and the sign of `smin` on the finite domain; it
+  did not formalize the Euler-Maclaurin identity.
+- Boxes versus windows. Each listed zero has a winding box of half-side
+  `0.0199995...` and a smaller Rouche disc. Two of the 1,268 boxes cross a
+  horizontal window border: row 615 (`t = 10700.01932412`, Rouche radius 1e-8)
+  and row 655 (`t = 11299.99212323`, Rouche radius 3e-9). Both Rouche discs lie
+  strictly inside their window, and the audit script checks this for all
+  1,268 rows. Window counts `N_R` come from the window contour, never from the
+  boxes, so box counts must not be equated with window counts; the script would
+  report a third border crossing as a failure.
+- The functional equation `Lambda_f(s) = Lambda_f(1-s)` with `Lambda_f = D f`,
+  `D(s) = (5/pi)^((s+1)/2) Gamma((s+1)/2)`, and the reality of `e^{i theta(t)} f(1/2+it)`
+  are what let on-line sign changes count zeros and let right-side zeros reflect
+  to the left. They follow from the Dirichlet functional equation for the odd
+  primitive characters mod 5 together with the exact identity
+  `(1 + i kappa)/(1 - i kappa) = epsilon_chi`, which reduces to
+  `kappa = (sqrt(10 - 2 sqrt 5) - 2)/(sqrt 5 - 1) = Im eps/(1 + Re eps)`. The
+  verifier only samples `imag.contains(0)` at separators; that sample is a
+  regression gate, not a proof of global reality. The identity above was
+  checked algebraically in review and numerically to 1.6e-16; it is cited here
+  as classical, not established by this repository's tests.
+
+## 4. The fault the pipeline rejects
+
+`lesion.py` loads the **original** package `vdh.py` by path and divides its
+`M_bound(0.5, 0.5, 1.25)` by 1,000. At `s = 7/4 + i/2` on that disc Arb proves
+`|f| > 0.99971325...` while the shrunken bound is `< 0.08366309...`; the

+# 47. The Davenport-Heilbronn zero, kernel-checked
+
+Riemann's zeta function satisfies a functional equation, `xi(s) = xi(1 - s)`, and all of
+its zeros that anyone has computed lie on the line Re s = 1/2. A natural question is
+whether the functional equation is what forces them there. In 1936 Davenport and
+Heilbronn answered no. They built a function with zeta's kind of Dirichlet series and an
+equally clean functional equation, which nonetheless has zeros off the line. Spira (1994)
+computed the lowest of them, near 0.808517 + 85.699348 i.
+
+This laboratory now has that fact as a theorem checked by Lean's kernel. This page says
+what was proved, how, and what it does and does not mean. The full record is hunt #145,
+`hunts/rung3_ball_production/` (`RESULTS.md` first).
+
+## 1. What is proved
+
+In Lean 4 (`v4.35.0-rc2`, Mathlib `065356127b1d`), with zero `sorry` and only the three
+standard axioms (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`), one theorem states the
+result:
+
+```lean
+theorem davenport_heilbronn_strip :
+    ∃ (f : ℂ → ℂ) (s : ℂ), Differentiable ℂ f ∧ dh_series_rep f ∧ dh_functional_eq f ∧
+      f s = 0 ∧ 0 < s.re ∧ s.re < 1 ∧ s.re ≠ 1/2
+```
+
+Some entire function, given by the Davenport-Heilbronn Dirichlet series for Re s > 1 and
+satisfying its functional equation, has a zero in the open critical strip off the line.
+The witness is `DH`. The theorem sits in its own module, downstream of the 215 sites, and
+bundles three theorems that, read together, carried the result before it:
+
+- `dh_analytic_half` (`lean/ZetaLean/DHAnalytic.lean`): this `DH`, built from the quartic
+  character mod 5, is entire, is given by the Davenport-Heilbronn Dirichlet series for
+  Re s > 1, and satisfies its functional equation.
+- `dh_zero_located`: a zero of `DH` lies in the closed square of half-width 3/64 about
+  808517/10^6 + (21424837/250000) i, so its real part is between 0.761642 and 0.855392.
+- `dh_separation_hundred`: below height 100, `DH` has a zero s with 0 < Re s < 1,
+  0 < Im s ≤ 100 and Re s ≠ 1/2, while every zero of Mathlib's `riemannZeta` in that
+  region has real part 1/2. The second half is hunt #137's RH to height 100 (`docs/45`).
+  This one says more than the bundled theorem, since it adds the comparison with zeta.
+
+The proof of `davenport_heilbronn_strip` takes the zero of `dh_zero_located` and the three
+facts behind `dh_analytic_half`. It was compiled on 2026-10-26 by a second assembly of the
+same 215 site oleans, whose earlier modules came out byte for byte as the first time. A
+statement broken in the strip condition, `Re s < 0.76` or a line through the square, was
+refused.
+
+The assembly also proves `davenport_heilbronn : davenport_heilbronn_statement`
+(`lean/ZetaLean/DavenportHeilbronn.lean`, line 129): some entire function with that
+series and functional equation has a zero s with Re s ≠ 1/2. **That statement, as
+defined, is also met by the trivial zero s = -1**, so it carries none of the result and
+needs none of the 215 sites. `DH` combines the L-functions of two odd characters, which
+vanish at s = -1, -3, -5, …, and `davenport_heilbronn_statement_of_trivial_zero`
+(`lean/ZetaLean/DHTrivialZero.lean`) proves the statement from `DH (-1) = 0` alone. The
+same statement for `riemannZeta` holds at its trivial zero s = -2. The adversarial review
+of PR #353 found this on 2026-10-26; the definition stays as it is because the 215 site
+oleans were compiled against the module that holds it.
+
+The grade of `davenport_heilbronn_strip` and the three theorems above is
+**kernel-checked, pending external verification**. No outside mathematician has reviewed them, and no independent kernel
+has replayed the assembled environment. Lean's own kernel did replay the whole closure
+into an empty environment on 2026-10-27 (`leanchecker --fresh`, 1.57 million constants,
+accepted in 7 h 17 min), a re-check by the same kernel rather than an independent one.
+
+## 2. How
+
+The analytic half (`DH` entire, its series and its functional equation), the tail bounds
+and a minimum-modulus criterion for a square were already kernel-checked in
+`lean/ZetaLean`. The criterion says: if `|DH|` is small at the square's centre and
+bounded below on its four edges, `DH` has a zero inside. What remained was numeric,
+about half a million literal facts about `DH` on the square's boundary.
+
+- **Plan v2** (`lean/cert/rung3_plan2.json`) covers it with 215 sites:
+  - 110 boxes on a larger square bound `|DH|` above, which bounds `DH'` on the small
+    square;
+  - 104 grid points on the small square's edges bound `|DH|` below;
+  - the centre bounds it above.
+- **Each site** is a generated Lean module tree that evaluates `DH` in ball arithmetic.
+  Every prime power `p^(-s)` is decided by the kernel in one step (`decide +kernel` on the
+  whole recursive ball value). That step cost about 1 CPU-s against about 66 for the
+  older staged form (`docs/37`, "Kernel evaluation by literal tables").
+- **The 215 sites** compiled on GitHub Actions in 16.1 core-hours, and one assembly module
+  combines their theorems through the criterion.
+- **Planted faults** were refused at the declaration they touch: a tower radius one unit
+  of 2^-64 low, a tail radius or a bound just under its target, and an eps' at the bound.
+
+## 3. What it means, and what it does not
+
+- **It shows the functional equation alone cannot give RH.** `davenport_heilbronn_strip`
+  says so in one statement: a function with zeta's kind of series and functional
+  equation has a zero in the open strip off the line. `dh_separation_hundred` adds that
+  the zero lies below a height where `riemannZeta` has none. Any proof of RH must use something zeta has and `DH` lacks,
+  such as the Euler product. This was known since 1936; what is new is that the
+  counterexample is now a kernel-checked theorem in this repository, usable as a battery
+  rival (`zeta.epstein.battery`, `docs/08` section 4) with its off-line zero proved
+  rather than computed. A rival must use these strip theorems, not
+  `davenport_heilbronn_statement`, whose analogue for zeta holds at a trivial zero.
+- **It says nothing about RH.** It is a statement about a different function.
+- **Prior art.** The lab produced it, so it is *original*. For a kernel-checked or
+  formally verified proof of a non-trivial Davenport-Heilbronn zero off the line, the
+  record is *searched-and-absent* in four web queries
+  (`hunts/rung3_ball_production/PRIOR_ART.md`, which lists what was not searched,
+  including zbMATH Open and the Lean Zulip). That is not a novelty claim.
+
+## 4. Doors
+
+The first door is an independent replay of the assembled environment by a second
+checker. It is cheapest before the site oleans' GitHub artifacts expire, about
+2026-11-25; after that it needs the 16 core-hours of sites again. The door beside it, one
+bundled theorem stating the strip result in a single declaration, is done: it is
+`davenport_heilbronn_strip` (section 1). The next is cheaper composites and terms by the same kernel decision. After
+those come Spira's next off-line zeros, at heights 114.16, 166.48 and 176.70, which need
+new plans. `hunts/rung3_ball_production/RESULTS.md`, "The doors", ranks them.

+### 8.10 PREREG (written 2026-10-26, before the run): the two-sided local gap
+
+Registered and pushed before `twosided.py` was run; the outcome is appended
+below it as section 8.11, whatever it is.
+
+**Model (zero free parameters).** For a pair at height gamma, depth y0, mean
+gap h = 2 pi / log(5 gamma / 2 pi): let d_L = gamma - (nearest line zero
+below gamma) and d_R = (nearest line zero above gamma) - gamma, from a line
+scan of the pair's own accounted window. Then
+
+    S2(y) = sum_{k=0}^{5999} [ 1/((d_L + k h)^2 + y^2) + 1/((d_R + k h)^2 + y^2) ],
+    t*_2  = int_0^{y0} y dy / (1 + 2 y^2 S2(y)),
+
+which is `theory.t_star_gap` exactly when d_L = d_R = DBAR h. One of d_L,
+d_R is the nearest line zero, and the other is the nearest on the other side.
+That other one is the second-nearest overall unless two line zeros sit on the
+same side closer than any on the other. How often that happens is recorded,
+and it does not change the model.
+
+**Data.** The 29 accounted, landed windows: 21 in `census_1e4.json` and 8 in
+`census_deep4_1e5.json`. The window at gamma = 88167.40 is excluded because
+its accounting is open. Line zeros come from `census_1e4.line_zeros` (grid
+1/60 mean gap, 30 bisections) on [gamma - 4h, gamma + 4h].
+
+**Gate (fixed in advance).** For every window, min(d_L, d_R) / h must
+reproduce the census's recorded `gap_ratio_d_over_h` to within 1e-4.
+Otherwise the run is void and nothing is graded.
+
+**Metric.** rms over the 29 of (ODE t* / t*_2 - 1), on the same footing as
+section 8.9's frozen-DBAR 0.160 and one-sided plug-in 0.393, with the same
+ODE landings and the same integral.
+
+**Pass/fail rule (fixed in advance).**
+
+- **PASS:** rms <= 0.080 (half the frozen value) *and* every one of the 29
+  ratios in [0.85, 1.25] (P3's band).
+- **IMPROVES, does not pass:** rms < 0.160 but not PASS.
+- **FAIL:** rms >= 0.160.
+
+A PASS supports, at measured grade, the reading that the gap correction is
+two-sided. It is not a theorem and says nothing about pairs near Delta,
+which no window here reaches. A FAIL refutes this form of it
+(ALIGNMENT section 5, disposition 1, at these 29 windows).

+"""Landing census below height 10^4: ODE landing times of the deepest pairs.
+
+Hunt #119, resumption of 2026-10-26, step 3 (coordinator-approved for 10^4
+only; 10^5 deferred).  Prediction P4 asks what a complete census to height
+10^4 does to the best measured landing 0.05765184035; P5, P6 and P8 ask where
+the maximum sits, what the local gap ratio is, and whether any pair lands
+later than its own y0^2/2.
+
+Candidates are the 21 zeros with beta > 0.85 below 10^4 (`decide_low_zeros.json`:
+positions decided on both backends; that they are *all* such zeros rests on
+the float screen and is measured).  A pair with y0 <= 0.35 needs
+y0^2/2 <= 0.06125 and so beats the floor only with a shave under 5.9 percent,
+against 12.5 to 16 percent measured at this depth in `hunts/lambda_dh_bounds`;
+they are not run, and that gap is stated rather than closed.
+
+Per candidate, deepest first, in the window [gamma - 40, gamma + 40]:
+
+1. line zeros: sign changes of the Hardy-style Z of f on a grid of 1/60 of
+   the mean gap, bisected 30 times (`deep_zeros.f_vline`, float64);
+2. N_right, the zeros with beta > 0.505, and N_strip, all zeros with
+   -1.05 < beta < 2.05, each by a float argument-principle count on the
+   rectangle (same evaluator); the accounting N_strip = N_line + 2 N_right
+   must close, else the window is recorded as unaccounted and not landed;
+3. the N_right off-line zeros located (grid minimum of |f| from beta = 0.51,
+   Newton), required distinct and equal in number to N_right;
+4. the landing: `hunts/flow_repair/probe.ode_null_control`, the N-body ODE
+   that `hunts/lambda_dh_bounds` matched to the Xi-plane contour measurement
+   within 0.04 percent on flow_repair pairs 1 to 5, with the same half-window
+   40 and 800 RK4 steps to t_end = 1.25 y0^2/2.
+
+Grade: every landing is *measured* (float route, one instrument).  The
+control is the floor pair itself (gamma = 240.4047): its ODE landing must
+reproduce the recorded 0.05765184035 to within the instrument's 0.04 percent
+band, or the census is not read.
+
+Run:  .venv/bin/python hunts/lambda_dh_exact/census_1e4.py [--only K] [--validate]
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import math
+import os
+import sys
+import time
+from fractions import Fraction
+
+import numpy as np
+
+_HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(_HERE))
+_FLOW = os.path.join(_ROOT, "hunts", "flow_repair")
+for _p in (_HERE, _ROOT, _FLOW):
+    if _p not in sys.path:
+        sys.path.insert(0, _p)
+
+import deep_zeros as dz  # noqa: E402
+import probe  # noqa: E402  (hunts/flow_repair/probe.py, read-only)
+
+SRC = os.path.join(_HERE, "decide_low_zeros.json")
+OUT = os.path.join(_HERE, "census_1e4.json")
+HALF = 40.0
+SIG_IN = 0.505
+SIG_ALL = -1.05
+SIG_FALLBACK = 0.5005
+FLOOR = 0.05765184034869543
+
+
+def _theta(t):
+    from scipy.special import loggamma
+    return np.imag(loggamma(0.75 + 0.5j * t)) - 0.5 * t * math.log(math.pi / 5)
+
+
+def line_zeros(a: float, b: float, per_gap: int = 60):
+    gap = probe.mean_gap(0.5 * (a + b))
+    npts = int(math.ceil((b - a) / gap * per_gap)) + 1
+    dt = (b - a) / (npts - 1)
+    ts = a + dt * np.arange(npts)
+    zz = np.real(np.exp(1j * _theta(ts)) * dz.f_vline(0.5, a, dt, npts))
+
+    def zed(t):
+        v = dz.f_one(complex(0.5, t))
+        th = float(_theta(np.array([t]))[0])
+        return math.cos(th) * v.real - math.sin(th) * v.imag
+
+    out = []
+    for i in range(npts - 1):
+        if (zz[i] > 0) != (zz[i + 1] > 0):
+            lo, hi, flo = ts[i], ts[i + 1], zz[i]
+            for _ in range(30):
+                m = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
+                fm = zed(m)
+                if (flo > 0) != (fm > 0):
+                    hi = m
+                else:
+                    lo, flo = m, fm
+            out.append(0.5 * (lo + hi))
+    return out
+
+
+def count_float(sig_c: float, a: float, b: float, pts_per_unit: int = 32):
+    """Measured argument-principle count on [sig_c, 2.05] x [a, b]."""
+    bottom = dz.hvariation(a, sa=sig_c, sb=dz.SIGMA_R, n=200)
+    top = dz.hvariation(b, sa=sig_c, sb=dz.SIGMA_R, n=200)
+    left, _ = dz.vline_variation(sig_c, a, b, pts_per_unit=pts_per_unit)
+    right, _ = dz.vline_variation(dz.SIGMA_R, a, b, pts_per_unit=pts_per_unit)
+    raw = (bottom + right - top - left) / (2 * math.pi)
+    n = int(round(raw))
+    return n, abs(raw - n)
+
+
+def _newton(seed: complex, a: float, b: float, iters: int = 60):
+    """Newton on the fast evaluator, abandoned as soon as it leaves the box."""
+    z = complex(seed)
+    h = 1e-6
+    for _ in range(iters):
+        if not (0.3 < z.real < 1.4 and a - 1 <= z.imag <= b + 1):
+            return None
+        fz = dz.f_one(z)
+        if abs(fz) < 1e-15:
+            return z
+        d = (dz.f_one(z + h) - dz.f_one(z - h)) / (2 * h)
+        if d == 0 or not np.isfinite(abs(d)):
+            return None
+        step = fz / d
+        if abs(step) > 0.5:
+            step *= 0.5 / abs(step)
+        z = z - step
+        if abs(step) < 1e-15:
+            return z
+    return z
+
+
+def offline_zeros(a: float, b: float, want: int, sig_in: float | None = None):
+    """Locate zeros with beta > sig_in (default SIG_IN) in [a, b]: grid minima, Newton, dedupe.
+
+    Below SIG_IN (the accounting fallback, added 2026-10-26) the grid gets extra
+    rows just right of sig_in, where a near-line pair lives.
+    """
+    sig_in = SIG_IN if sig_in is None else sig_in
+    found = []
+    xs = np.linspace(sig_in + 0.005, 1.15, 24)
+    if sig_in < SIG_IN:
+        xs = np.concatenate([np.linspace(sig_in + 0.0003, SIG_IN + 0.004, 8), xs])
+    step = 0.05
+    npts = int((b - a) / step) + 1
+    grid = np.array([np.abs(dz.f_vline(float(x), a, step, npts)) for x in xs])
+    # local minima of |f| over the 2-D grid, best first
+    cand = []
+    for i in range(len(xs)):
+        for j in range(1, npts - 1):
+            v = grid[i, j]
+            lo_i, hi_i = max(0, i - 1), min(len(xs), i + 2)
+            if v <= grid[lo_i:hi_i, j - 1:j + 2].min():
+                cand.append((v, complex(xs[i], a + step * j)))
+    cand.sort(key=lambda c: c[0])
+    for _, seed in cand:
+        z = _newton(seed, a, b)
+        if z is None or not (sig_in < z.real < 1.2 and a <= z.imag <= b):
+            continue
+        if abs(dz.f_one(z)) > 1e-9:
+            continue
+        if any(abs(z - w) < 1e-6 for w in found):
+            continue
+        found.append(z)
+        if len(found) >= want + 3:
+            break
+    return found
+
+
+def census_one(gamma: float, y0: float) -> dict:
+    t0 = time.time()
+    a, b = gamma - HALF, gamma + HALF
+    # nudge the window edges off any zero: choose edges at line-grid midpoints
+    reals = line_zeros(a - 1.0, b + 1.0)
+    inner = [r for r in reals if a <= r <= b]
+    if inner:
+        lo_gap = [r for r in reals if r < a]
+        hi_gap = [r for r in reals if r > b]
+        if lo_gap:
+            a = 0.5 * (lo_gap[-1] + inner[0])
+        if hi_gap:
+            b = 0.5 * (inner[-1] + hi_gap[0])
+    reals = [r for r in reals if a < r < b]
+    n_right, d_right = count_float(SIG_IN, a, b)
+    n_all, d_all = count_float(SIG_ALL, a, b)
+    entry = {"gamma": gamma, "y0": y0, "window": [a, b],
+             "n_line": len(reals), "n_right_beta_gt_0.505": n_right,
+             "defect_right": d_right, "n_strip": n_all, "defect_strip": d_all}
+    entry["accounting_ok"] = bool(n_all == len(reals) + 2 * n_right)
+    if not entry["accounting_ok"]:
+        reals = line_zeros(a, b, per_gap=240)
+        entry["n_line_refined"] = len(reals)
+        entry["accounting_ok"] = bool(n_all == len(reals) + 2 * n_right)
+    sig_used = SIG_IN
+    if not entry["accounting_ok"]:
+        # Fallback (2026-10-26, hunt #119 unit 4): a pair with beta in
+        # (SIG_FALLBACK, SIG_IN) makes no line sign change and is not counted
+        # at SIG_IN; the window at gamma = 88167.40 held one at beta 0.50479.
+        n_fb, d_fb = count_float(SIG_FALLBACK, a, b)
+        entry["accounting_fallback"] = {"sig_in": SIG_FALLBACK, "n_right": n_fb, "defect": d_fb}
+        if n_all == len(reals) + 2 * n_fb:
+            entry["accounting_ok"] = True
+            n_right, sig_used = n_fb, SIG_FALLBACK
+    entry["sig_in_used"] = sig_used
+    offl = offline_zeros(a, b, n_right, sig_used)
+    entry["n_offline_located"] = len(offl)
+    entry["offline_located_ok"] = bool(len(offl) == n_right)
+    me = min(offl, key=lambda z: abs(z - complex(0.5 + y0, gamma))) if offl else None
+    entry["self_found"] = bool(me is not None and abs(me - complex(0.5 + y0, gamma)) < 1e-6)
+    others = [{"x": z.imag, "y": z.real - 0.5} for z in offl if me is None or abs(z - me) > 1e-6]
+    entry["other_pairs"] = [[o["x"], o["y"]] for o in others]
+    near = min(reals, key=lambda r: abs(complex(0.5, r) - complex(0.5 + y0, gamma)))
+    entry["nearest_line_zero_distance"] = abs(complex(0.5, near) - complex(0.5 + y0, gamma))
+    entry["gap_ratio_d_over_h"] = abs(near - gamma) / probe.mean_gap(gamma)
+    entry["landing_naive"] = y0 * y0 / 2
+    if entry["accounting_ok"] and entry["offline_located_ok"] and entry["self_found"]:
+        ode = probe.ode_null_control({"gamma": gamma, "y0": y0}, reals, others,
+                                     t_end=1.25 * y0 * y0 / 2, n_steps=800, window=HALF)
+        entry["landing_ode"] = ode["tstar_ode"]
+        entry["shave_percent"] = (100 * (1 - ode["tstar_ode"] / (y0 * y0 / 2))
+                                  if ode["tstar_ode"] else None)
+        # the ODE matches the Xi-plane measurement to 0.04 percent, so a landing
+        # only beats the measured floor if it clears that band
+        #
+        # KNOWN LIMIT (recorded 2026-10-26 in review, RESULTS.md section 8.16;
+        # logic deliberately unchanged): when the pair has not landed by
+        # t_end = 1.25 y0^2/2, probe.ode_null_control returns tstar_ode None,
+        # and this row then gets landing_ode None, beats_floor False and
+        # later_than_naive False.  For y0 > 0.3396, t_end exceeds 0.072, above
+        # the floor, so the one row that would beat the floor most reads as
+        # not beating it.  evaluate_census.py then drops it from its landed
+        # rows.  It did not occur in any recorded census (every row landed,
+        # pinned by test_known_limit_no_crossing_reads_as_not_beating_the_floor
+        # and the census2 tests).
+        entry["beats_floor"] = bool(ode["tstar_ode"] and ode["tstar_ode"] > FLOOR * 1.0004)
+        entry["later_than_naive"] = bool(ode["tstar_ode"] and ode["tstar_ode"] > y0 * y0 / 2)
+        entry["ode"] = {k: v for k, v in ode.items() if k != "trajectory_Q"}
+    else:
+        entry["landing_ode"] = None
+        entry["skipped"] = "accounting or location did not close; not landed"
+    entry["seconds"] = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
+    return entry
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument("--only", type=int, default=None, help="run only the K deepest")
+    ap.add_argument("--index", type=int, default=None, help="run one candidate by depth rank")
+    ap.add_argument("--out", default=OUT)
+    ap.add_argument("--source", default=None,
+                    help="a deep_zeros screen artifact with a 'zeros' list (float locations) "
+                         "instead of the decided low zeros")
+    ap.add_argument("--min-y0", type=float, default=0.0,
+                    help="with --source: land only zeros deeper than this")
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+    cands = []
+    if args.source:
+        for z in json.load(open(args.source))["zeros"]:
+            if z["y0"] > args.min_y0:
+                cands.append((z["y0"], z["gamma"]))
+    else:
+        for r in json.load(open(SRC))["rows"]:
+            lo, hi = r["y0_enclosure_float"]
+            tl, th = (float(Fraction(x)) for x in r["rectangle_t"])
+            cands.append((0.5 * (lo + hi), 0.5 * (tl + th)))
+    cands.sort(key=lambda c: -c[0])
+    if args.index is not None:
+        cands = [cands[args.index]]
+    elif args.only:
+        cands = cands[: args.only]
+    data = json.load(open(args.out)) if os.path.exists(args.out) else {"rows": []}
+    done = {round(e["gamma"], 3) for e in data["rows"]}
+    for y0, g in cands:
+        if round(g, 3) in done:
+            continue
+        e = census_one(g, y0)
+        data["rows"].append(e)
+        data["rows"].sort(key=lambda r: r["gamma"])
+        with open(args.out, "w") as fh:
+            json.dump(data, fh, indent=2)
+        print(f"gamma {g:.4f} y0 {y0:.6f} line {e['n_line']} right {e['n_right_beta_gt_0.505']} "
+              f"strip {e['n_strip']} acct {e['accounting_ok']} located {e['n_offline_located']} "
+              f"t*_ode {e['landing_ode']} naive {e['landing_naive']:.6f} [{e['seconds']}s]", flush=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""Sharded landing census over [10^4, 10^5], for GitHub Actions.
+
+Hunt #119, unit 3 (2026-10-26).  Driven by `.github/workflows/lambda-dh-census.yml`,
+which runs only when `RUN_REQUEST.json` is pushed to this branch (it is not
+committed until the coordinator says go). The pre-registration is
+`RESULTS.md` section 8.12.
+
+Per shard (a height interval of `census_plan_1e5.json`):
+
+1. screen the interval at Re s = 0.82 (`deep_zeros.py screen`, checkpointed),
+2. locate the flagged windows (`deep_zeros.py locate`),
+3. land every located zero with y0 > 0.3396 (`census_1e4.py --source`, which
+   skips rows already present: the resume),
+4. write `shard_<i>.json` with the plan hash and per-stage CPU seconds.
+
+Subcommands:
+
+    plan       write census_plan_1e5.json and print its sha256 (committed)
+    preflight  fail closed: pinned versions, ball backend, plan hash against
+               RUN_REQUEST.json, and a smoke check (one committed census_1e4
+               row recomputed and compared)
+    run        one shard (--shard i), resumable
+    gather     per shard, copy the most advanced copy among several downloaded
+               attempts (subdirectories of --src) into --out
+    merge      fold shard files into census_1e5.json, refusing a missing shard
+               or a shard from another plan
+    calib      summarize a calibration shard: CPU seconds per screened 20-unit
+               window and per census window, and the projected core-hours
+
+Grade of everything it produces: *measured* (float screen, ODE landings).
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+import math
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import time
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(HERE))
+PLAN = os.path.join(HERE, "census_plan_1e5.json")
+REQUEST = os.path.join(HERE, "RUN_REQUEST.json")
+PINS = os.path.join(HERE, "census_constraints.txt")
+
+T0, T1 = 10000, 100000
+SHARD_WIDTH = 2500            # 36 shards; a multiple of the 20-unit screen window
+SIGMA_C = 0.82
+MIN_Y0 = 0.3396               # y0^2/2 > 0.0576518 needs y0 > 0.33957
+SMOKE_GAMMA = 240.4047        # the floor pair: census_1e4.json control row
+SMOKE_RTOL = 1e-6
+
+
+def canonical(obj) -> bytes:
+    return json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
+
+
+def plan_obj() -> dict:
+    shards = [[T0 + SHARD_WIDTH * i, T0 + SHARD_WIDTH * (i + 1)]
+              for i in range((T1 - T0) // SHARD_WIDTH)]
+    return {"what": "hunt #119 census [1e4, 1e5]", "sigma_c": SIGMA_C, "min_y0": MIN_Y0,
+            "census_half_window": 40.0, "ode_steps": 800, "shards": shards}
+
+
+def plan_sha(path: str | None = None) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(canonical(json.load(open(path or PLAN)))).hexdigest()
+
+
+def stage_plan() -> None:
+    with open(PLAN, "w") as fh:
+        json.dump(plan_obj(), fh, indent=1)
+        fh.write("\n")
+    print(plan_sha())
+
+
+def _pins() -> dict:
+    out = {}
+    for line in open(PINS):
+        line = line.split("#")[0].strip()
+        if line:
+            name, ver = line.split("==")
+            out[name.strip().lower()] = ver.strip()
+    return out
+
+
+def stage_preflight() -> None:
+    from importlib.metadata import version
+    pins = _pins()
+    for name, ver in pins.items():
+        got = version(name)
+        if got != ver:
+            raise SystemExit(f"preflight: {name} {got} != pinned {ver}")
+    sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)
+    from zeta import rigor
+    if rigor.BACKEND != "python-flint":
+        raise SystemExit(f"preflight: ball backend {rigor.BACKEND}")
+    req = json.load(open(REQUEST))
+    if req.get("plan_sha256") != plan_sha():
+        raise SystemExit("preflight: RUN_REQUEST plan_sha256 does not match census_plan_1e5.json")
+    if PLAN == os.path.join(HERE, "census_plan_1e5.json") and plan_obj() != json.load(open(PLAN)):
+        raise SystemExit("preflight: census_plan_1e5.json differs from the plan this code generates")
+    if req.get("mode") not in ("calibrate", "full"):
+        raise SystemExit(f"preflight: mode {req.get('mode')!r}")
+    # smoke: recompute the committed control row and compare
+    sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
+    import census_1e4 as cz
+    rec = next(r for r in json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, "census_1e4.json")))["rows"]
+               if abs(r["gamma"] - SMOKE_GAMMA) < 1e-3)
+    got = cz.census_one(rec["gamma"], rec["y0"])
+    for k in ("n_line", "n_strip", "n_right_beta_gt_0.505"):
+        if got[k] != rec[k]:
+            raise SystemExit(f"preflight smoke: {k} {got[k]} != recorded {rec[k]}")
+    if abs(got["landing_ode"] / rec["landing_ode"] - 1) > SMOKE_RTOL:
+        raise SystemExit(f"preflight smoke: landing {got['landing_ode']} vs {rec['landing_ode']}")
+    print(json.dumps({"preflight": "ok", "pins": pins, "plan_sha256": plan_sha(),
+                      "smoke_landing": got["landing_ode"], "smoke_seconds": got["seconds"]}))
+
+
+def _cpu(cmd: list[str]) -> float:
+    """Run cmd to completion; return its user + sys CPU seconds."""
+    before = os.times()
+    subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)
+    after = os.times()
+    return (after.children_user - before.children_user) + (after.children_system - before.children_system)
+
+
+def peak_rss_gb() -> dict:
+    """Peak resident set sizes in GiB (Linux ru_maxrss is in KiB).
+
+    The shard's work runs in child processes (screen, locate, census), so
+    RUSAGE_SELF alone measures only this driver. RUSAGE_CHILDREN is the peak
+    of the largest child waited for so far, and the peak is the larger of the two.
+    """
+    import resource
+    me = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss / 2**20
+    kids = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN).ru_maxrss / 2**20
+    return {"self_gb": me, "children_gb": kids, "peak_gb": max(me, kids)}
+
+
+def stage_run(i: int, out_dir: str) -> None:
+    plan = json.load(open(PLAN))
+    t0, t1 = plan["shards"][i]
+    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
+    screen = os.path.join(out_dir, f"screen_{i}.json")
+    census = os.path.join(out_dir, f"census_{i}.json")
+    summary = os.path.join(out_dir, f"shard_{i}.json")
+    py = sys.executable
+    dz = os.path.join(HERE, "deep_zeros.py")
+    cpu = {}
+    cpu["screen"] = _cpu([py, dz, "screen", "--t0", str(t0), "--t1", str(t1), "--sigma-c", str(SIGMA_C),
+                          "--out", screen, "--key", "screen_c82"])
+    cpu["locate"] = _cpu([py, dz, "locate", "--sigma-c", str(SIGMA_C), "--out", screen, "--key", "screen_c82"])
+    cpu["census"] = _cpu([py, os.path.join(HERE, "census_1e4.py"), "--source", screen,
+                          "--min-y0", str(plan["min_y0"]), "--out", census])
+    sc = json.load(open(screen))
+    rows = json.load(open(census))["rows"] if os.path.exists(census) else []
+    n_cand = sum(z["y0"] > plan["min_y0"] for z in sc.get("zeros", []))
+    # CPU accumulates across resumed runs, so a calibration read after a
+    # resume still sees the whole cost of the shard
+    prev = json.load(open(summary))["cpu_seconds"] if os.path.exists(summary) else {}
+    runs = (json.load(open(summary)).get("runs", 1) + 1) if os.path.exists(summary) else 1
+    cpu = {k: cpu[k] + prev.get(k, 0.0) for k in cpu}
+    rss = peak_rss_gb()
+    prev_rss = json.load(open(summary)).get("peak_rss", {}) if os.path.exists(summary) else {}
+    rss["peak_gb"] = max(rss["peak_gb"], prev_rss.get("peak_gb", 0.0))
+    body = {"shard": i, "interval": [t0, t1], "plan_sha256": plan_sha(), "runs": runs,
+            "screen_complete": sc["screen_c82"]["complete"],
+            "n_screen_windows": len(sc["screen_c82"]["boundaries"]) - 1,
+            "n_located": len(sc.get("zeros", [])), "n_candidates": n_cand,
+            "n_unlocated": len(sc.get("unlocated", [])), "unlocated": sc.get("unlocated", []),
+            "n_relocated_by_guard": sum(bool(z.get("guard", {}).get("first_root_refused"))
+                                        for z in sc.get("zeros", [])),
+            "n_accounting_fallback": sum("accounting_fallback" in r for r in rows),
+            "n_landed": sum(r["landing_ode"] is not None for r in rows),
+            "n_unaccounted": sum(not r["accounting_ok"] for r in rows),
+            "cpu_seconds": cpu, "peak_rss": rss, "finished": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())}
+    with open(summary, "w") as fh:
+        json.dump(body, fh, indent=1)
+    print(json.dumps(body))
+
+
+def stage_calib(out_dir: str, i: int = 0) -> None:
+    s = json.load(open(os.path.join(out_dir, f"shard_{i}.json")))
+    per_screen = (s["cpu_seconds"]["screen"] + s["cpu_seconds"]["locate"]) / max(1, s["n_screen_windows"])
+    per_census = s["cpu_seconds"]["census"] / max(1, s["n_candidates"])
+    plan = json.load(open(PLAN))
+    n_windows = (T1 - T0) // 20
+    # candidate count scales with the shard's share of the decade; one shard is a lower-precision sample
+    n_cand = s["n_candidates"] * len(plan["shards"])
+    # less noisy: the decade's 111 zeros at Re s > 0.85 (deep_zeros_hi_20261026.json,
+    # measured) scaled by this shard's ratio of candidates to those
+    hi = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, "deep_zeros_hi_20261026.json")))["zeros"]
+    t0, t1 = s["interval"]
+    n85_here = sum(t0 <= z["gamma"] < t1 for z in hi)
+    n_cand_scaled = (len(hi) * s["n_candidates"] / n85_here) if n85_here else None
+    total = per_screen * n_windows + per_census * n_cand
+    out = {"cpu_s_per_screen_window": per_screen, "cpu_s_per_census_window": per_census,
+           "projected_candidates": n_cand, "projected_core_hours": total / 3600,
+           "n_085_zeros_in_shard": n85_here, "projected_candidates_scaled": n_cand_scaled,
+           "projected_core_hours_scaled": (per_screen * n_windows + per_census * n_cand_scaled) / 3600
+           if n_cand_scaled is not None else None,
+           "peak_rss_gb": s["peak_rss"]["peak_gb"],
+           "four_x_peak_rss_gb": 4 * s["peak_rss"]["peak_gb"],
+           "four_x_peak_rss_ok_13gb": 4 * s["peak_rss"]["peak_gb"] <= 13.0,
+           "from_shard": s}
+    with open(os.path.join(out_dir, "calibration.json"), "w") as fh:
+        json.dump(out, fh, indent=1)
+    print(json.dumps(out, indent=1))
+
+
+def _progress(d: str, i: int) -> tuple:
+    """How far a copy of shard i got: (summary present, screen complete, landed, runs, screen size)."""
+    summ = os.path.join(d, f"shard_{i}.json")
+    screen = os.path.join(d, f"screen_{i}.json")
+    census = os.path.join(d, f"census_{i}.json")
+    landed = len(json.load(open(census))["rows"]) if os.path.exists(census) else 0
+    if os.path.exists(summ):
+        sm = json.load(open(summ))
+        return (1, int(sm["screen_complete"]), landed, sm.get("runs", 1), 0)
+    size = os.path.getsize(screen) if os.path.exists(screen) else 0
+    return (0, 0, landed, 0, size)
+
+
+def stage_gather(src: str, out_dir: str) -> None:

+    for k in range(nblocks):

+    return (SIGMA_C < rho.real < SIGMA_R) and (ta - BOX_TOL <= rho.imag <= tb + BOX_TOL)

+Output: `census_runs/full_r1/evaluation.json`.

+    import census_1e4 as cz

+    reals = cz.line_zeros(g - 4 * h, g + 4 * h)

+"""The shave model with each pair's own local gap: a per-pair d/h refit.
+
+Hunt #119, follow-up of 2026-10-26, the door `RESULTS.md` section 8.7 named:
+the calibrated model `theory.t_star_gap(y0, gamma, dfac)` freezes the local
+gap at DBAR = 1.4284 mean gaps for every pair, and its four large misses
+(ODE / model < 0.7) all sit at measured d/h < 0.123.  This module asks two
+things of the 29 ODE landings (`census_1e4.json`, `census_deep4_1e5.json`):
+
+1. **plug-in**: the model with dfac = the pair's own measured d/h (distance
+   from the pair's ordinate to the nearest line zero over 2 pi / log(5 gamma /
+   2 pi)), against the ODE landing;
+2. **inverse**: the dfac that makes the model reproduce the ODE landing
+   exactly (brentq), against the measured d/h.
+
+Grade: *measured* (float, one model, landings themselves measured).  Nothing
+here is a fit with more than zero free parameters per pair in (1); (2) is a
+diagnostic, not a model.
+
+Run:  .venv/bin/python hunts/lambda_dh_exact/refit_dh.py
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import math
+import os
+import time
+
+from scipy.optimize import brentq
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+OUT = os.path.join(HERE, "refit_dh.json")
+
+
+def _theory():
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("ldh_theory", os.path.join(HERE, "theory.py"))
+    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
+    return mod
+
+
+def _rows():
+    out = []
+    for name in ("census_1e4.json", "census_deep4_1e5.json"):
+        for r in json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, name)))["rows"]:
+            if r["landing_ode"] is not None:
+                out.append((name, r))
+    return out
+
+
+def _stats(xs):
+    m = sum(xs) / len(xs)
+    rms = math.sqrt(sum((x - 1) ** 2 for x in xs) / len(xs))
+    return {"mean": m, "rms_dev_from_1": rms, "min": min(xs), "max": max(xs)}
+
+
+def _linear(pairs):
+    """Least squares d_inverse = a + b d_measured, with residual rms and max."""
+    n = len(pairs)
+    mx = sum(x for x, _ in pairs) / n
+    my = sum(y for _, y in pairs) / n
+    b = sum((x - mx) * (y - my) for x, y in pairs) / sum((x - mx) ** 2 for x, _ in pairs)
+    a = my - b * mx
+    res = [y - (a + b * x) for x, y in pairs]
+    return {"a": a, "b": b, "rms_resid": math.sqrt(sum(r * r for r in res) / n),
+            "max_abs_resid": max(abs(r) for r in res)}
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    t0 = time.time()
+    th = _theory()
+    rows = []
+    for src, r in _rows():
+        y0, g, tode, dh = r["y0"], r["gamma"], r["landing_ode"], r["gap_ratio_d_over_h"]
+        m_frozen = float(th.t_star_gap(y0, g))
+        m_plug = float(th.t_star_gap(y0, g, dfac=dh))
+        f = lambda d: float(th.t_star_gap(y0, g, dfac=d)) - tode
+        try:
+            d_inv = brentq(f, 1e-3, 20.0, xtol=1e-8)
+        except ValueError:
+            d_inv = None
+        rows.append({"source": src, "gamma": g, "y0": y0, "landing_ode": tode,
+                     "d_over_h_measured": dh, "model_frozen_dbar": m_frozen,
+                     "ratio_frozen": tode / m_frozen, "model_plugin": m_plug,
+                     "ratio_plugin": tode / m_plug, "d_over_h_inverse": d_inv})
+    rf = [r["ratio_frozen"] for r in rows]
+    rp = [r["ratio_plugin"] for r in rows]
+    inv = [(r["d_over_h_measured"], r["d_over_h_inverse"]) for r in rows if r["d_over_h_inverse"]]
+    mx = sum(a for a, _ in inv) / len(inv)
+    my = sum(b for _, b in inv) / len(inv)
+    cov = sum((a - mx) * (b - my) for a, b in inv)
+    corr = cov / math.sqrt(sum((a - mx) ** 2 for a, _ in inv) * sum((b - my) ** 2 for _, b in inv))
+    out = {
+        "what": "shave model with per-pair measured d/h vs frozen DBAR, against 29 ODE landings",
+        "date": "2026-10-26", "DBAR": th.DBAR, "n": len(rows),
+        "frozen": _stats(rf), "plugin": _stats(rp),
+        "inverse_vs_measured": {"n": len(inv), "pearson_r": corr,
+                                "mean_inverse": my, "mean_measured": mx,
+                                "linear_fit": _linear(inv)},
+        "plugin_ratio_above_1": sum(x > 1 for x in rp),
+        "rows": rows, "seconds": round(time.time() - t0, 1),
+    }
+    with open(OUT, "w") as fh:
+        json.dump(out, fh, indent=2)
+    print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in out.items() if k != "rows"}, indent=1))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""Find the true zero in each window that `deep_zeros.stage_locate` mislocated.
+
+Hunt #119, unit 3 (2026-10-26), diagnostic for the census's K-d failure
+(RUNS.md Run 17). `census_runs/full_r1/mislocated.json` lists 17 flagged
+windows whose accepted root lies outside the counted box beta > sigma_c. For
+each one: a float count on [sigma_c, 2.05] x window (must be 1, as the screen
+said), then a search constrained to the box (grid minima of |f| from
+beta = sigma_c + 0.005, Newton abandoned outside the box), keeping a root only
+if it lies strictly inside it.
+
+Grade: *measured*, diagnostic. It does not repair the census, which stays
+void as registered (RESULTS.md section 8.12, K-d).
+
+Run:  .venv/bin/python hunts/lambda_dh_exact/relocate_missed.py
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+import time
+
+import numpy as np
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+if HERE not in sys.path:
+    sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
+
+import census_1e4 as cz  # noqa: E402
+import deep_zeros as dz  # noqa: E402
+
+SRC = os.path.join(HERE, "census_runs", "full_r1", "mislocated.json")
+OUT = os.path.join(HERE, "census_runs", "full_r1", "relocated.json")
+
+
+def search(sig_c: float, a: float, b: float):
+    xs = np.linspace(sig_c + 0.005, 1.15, 24)
+    step = 0.05
+    npts = int((b - a) / step) + 1
+    grid = np.array([np.abs(dz.f_vline(float(x), a, step, npts)) for x in xs])
+    cand = []
+    for i in range(len(xs)):
+        for j in range(1, npts - 1):
+            lo_i, hi_i = max(0, i - 1), min(len(xs), i + 2)
+            if grid[i, j] <= grid[lo_i:hi_i, j - 1:j + 2].min():
+                cand.append((grid[i, j], complex(xs[i], a + step * j)))
+    cand.sort(key=lambda c: c[0])
+    found = []
+    for _, seed in cand[:40]:
+        z = cz._newton(seed, a, b)
+        if z is None or not (sig_c < z.real < 1.2 and a < z.imag < b):
+            continue
+        if abs(dz.f_one(z)) > 1e-9 or any(abs(z - w) < 1e-6 for w in found):
+            continue
+        found.append(z)
+    return found
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    t0 = time.time()
+    rows = []
+    for m in json.load(open(SRC))["rows"]:
+        tw = time.time()
+        a, b = m["window"]
+        n, defect = cz.count_float(m["sigma_c"], a, b)
+        found = search(m["sigma_c"], a, b)
+        rows.append({**m, "count_in_box": n, "count_defect": defect,
+                     "found": [{"gamma": z.imag, "beta": z.real, "y0": z.real - 0.5} for z in found],
+                     "ok": n == len(found) == 1, "seconds": round(time.time() - tw, 1)})
+        f = rows[-1]["found"]
+        print(m["source"], m["window"], "count", n, "found",
+              [(round(x["gamma"], 2), round(x["y0"], 4)) for x in f], f"[{rows[-1]['seconds']}s]", flush=True)
+    ok = [r for r in rows if r["ok"]]
+    out = {"what": "true zeros of the mislocated windows, constrained search (measured)",
+           "n": len(rows), "n_ok": len(ok),
+           "max_y0_found": max((r["found"][0]["y0"] for r in ok), default=None),
+           "n_y0_gt_0.3396": sum(r["found"][0]["y0"] > 0.3396 for r in ok),
+           "n_y0_gt_0.40": sum(r["found"][0]["y0"] > 0.40 for r in ok),
+           "rows": rows, "seconds": round(time.time() - t0, 1)}
+    with open(OUT, "w") as fh:
+        json.dump(out, fh, indent=1)
+    print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in out.items() if k != "rows"}, indent=1))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
